Japanese-Speaking Researcher      
 
   Hybrid Work Arrangement |      
   Attractive Remuneration |       
   Friendly & Supportive Team Environment      
 
  An exceptional opportunity is available to join a prestigious global organisation offering a flexible hybrid work model, excellent benefits, and a collaborative work environment.     
  In this role, you will research, translate, analyse, and summarise Australian news and current affairs content in Japanese for reporting to Head Office. Coverage areas include Australia-Japan relations, politics, economics, public policy, and geopolitical developments across Australia, New Zealand, and the Pacific Islands.     
  If you have experience in research, media monitoring, policy analysis, journalism, or related fields, we would love to hear from you.     
   Key Responsibilities      
 
  Conduct research and prepare concise reports, summaries, presentations, and briefings (Word, PowerPoint, etc.) for Head Office.     
  Monitor and analyse political, economic, and geopolitical developments across Australia, New Zealand, and the Pacific region.     
  Research industry developments in:      
  Critical minerals and mining     
  Energy (natural gas, coal, CCS)     
  Infrastructure (power, utilities, data centres, social infrastructure)     
  Food and agribusiness     
  Track and report on Australian foreign policy, including:      
  Australia's engagement with the Pacific and ASEAN     
  Australian Politics and Economy     
  Australia-Japan relations     
  Australia-Japan-United States trilateral cooperation     
  Attend seminars, conferences, and stakeholder meetings, and prepare timely meeting notes and summary reports in Japanese.     
  Build and maintain relationships with external experts, including think tanks, academic institutions, and industry specialists.     
  Manage external research projects and coordinate with outsourced research providers to ensure high-quality deliverables.     
  Travel within Australia, Pacific Island countries, and Japan as required, and prepare reports on findings and activities.     
  Liaise closely with Head Office regarding research activities and intelligence gathering.     
  Perform additional duties and special projects as required.     
 
   About You      
 
  Native-level or business-fluent Japanese with excellent Japanese writing and reporting skills.     
  Experience researching, analysing, translating, or summarising news articles, policy developments, or market intelligence is highly desirable.     
  Background in journalism, media, research, government, consulting, public policy, international relations, economics, or a related field will be highly regarded.     
  Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.     
  Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.     
  Unlimited Australian work rights (Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident, or Partner Visa holder).     
 
   What's on Offer      
 
  Competitive salary package.     
  Hybrid work arrangement (office and work-from-home flexibility).     
  Opportunity to work with a respected global organisation.     
  Exposure to international policy, business, and geopolitical issues.     
  Supportive, friendly, and collaborative working environment.     
  Domestic and international travel opportunities.     
 
  If you're passionate about research, current affairs, and Japan-Australia relations, we encourage you to apply.  career@ssb.hoban.com.au

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Located in: Sydney
Employment type: Fixed Term (FT-PT)
Hours: Full-time (38 hours per week), opportunity for Part-Time employment

Help shape care without the hospital trek. 

St Vincent's Health Australia is bringing care home. Through our Care at Home portfolio, we are reshaping how care is delivered - extending hospital-grade care beyond our walls and into communities, homes and virtual settings that meets people where they are.

Our Care at Home portfolio is scaling rapidly, enabling 24-7 connected care, smarter systems and care that feels more personal, more compassionate and more human.

St Vincent's Care at Home is seeking an experienced Physiotherapist to join our Rehab at Home program in Sydney. This role delivers high-quality rehabilitation to patients in their own homes, supporting safe early discharge and recovery following elective orthopaedic surgery and acute private hospital admissions to St Vincent's Mater and Sydney Private hospitals.

Rehab at Home is an established, evidence-based model combining in-home physiotherapy, virtual care, and multidisciplinary coordination to achieve excellent patient outcomes while avoiding unnecessary hospital stays.

About You

You'll bring expert physiotherapy care into the community with confident autonomous practice, sharp clinical reasoning, and a modern, tech-enabled approach to rehabilitation.

You Bring 

AHPRA-registered Physiotherapist

Non-negotiable: Minimum 3 years of experience

Desirable: Experience in rehabilitation, orthopaedics, subacute or community care

Confident working autonomously in home-based settings

Strong clinical reasoning, communication and time-management skills

Comfortable using digital tools and telehealth as part of routine care

Current driver's licence and access to a suitable motor vehicle

Join the St Vincent's family and access to

Growth & development
Access ongoing learning, professional development and industry-leading educational partnerships across NSW, VIC and QLD.

Salary sacrifice
As a not-for-profit provider, we offer generous salary packaging - enabling part of your salary to be taken home tax-free, including access to a meal-entitlement card.

Discounts, health and wellbeing
Access a range of employee perks including discounted gym memberships and our free 24-7 staff counselling and wellbeing service.

Workplace giving
Opportunities to engage in volunteering and community programs, including paid volunteering leave and workplace giving initiatives.

Why St Vincent's?

You'll love where health is heading.

At St Vincent's, we're combining the power of technology with the humanity of our people - building a system that gives:

People more choice, connection and care at home

Clinicians more time to care, connect and share their expertise

Our teams new opportunities to grow, lead and innovate

Ready to Apply?

If you're excited by digitally enabled care, motivated by purpose and ready to help shape a better, fairer system, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply with your CV and cover letter. Applications may close early.

Important Information

Employment is subject to pre-employment checks, including relevant immunisations.
 

We celebrate diversity and inclusion and are committed to equal opportunity for everyone.

Due to their expanding international footprint of advisors and corporate offices spanning Melbourne, Queensland, and Dubai, their infrastructure requires enterprise-grade engineering and now seek an experienced Computer?Network and System Engineer to join the team in Hampton East, Victoria. 

?? 

The Role:

? 

The Responsibilities: 

Design, deploy, and manage secure, high-availability Local Area Networks (LAN), Wide Area Networks (WAN), and wireless environments across all corporate offices, including Hampton East (VIC), Mermaid Beach (QLD), and Dubai. 

Implement advanced networking technologies and configure routers, firewalls, and network switches to prioritise high-bandwidth traffic, ensuring seamless VoIP communication.  

Create, update, and maintain detailed technical documentation, including network inventories, configuration change logs, maintenance procedures, and fault resolution records. 

Design and deploy network configurations, incorporating high-availability routing protocols, Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs), Quality of Service (QoS) rules, and secure site-to-site VPN tunnels. 

Implement SoftwareDefined Networking (SDN) and develop programmatic, APIdriven workflows across network hardware using automation tools such as PowerShell, Bash, Python, and RESTful integrations to improve operational efficiency and system reliability. 

Monitor and analyse network traffic, capacity, and utilisation metrics, and evaluate endtoend network infrastructure performance across all corporate office locations. 

Evaluate and propose technical enhancements to network operations, interconnected server infrastructure, internal hardware, distributed PropTech applications, and hybrid operational environments. 

Optimise 4K media-rendering architectures and secure localised Network attached Storage (NAS) configurations, improving internal high-volume data-pipeline workflows for the marketing division. 

Oversee network and system configurations to ensure smooth data flows between real estate-specific APIs, external listing syndications (e.g., Realestate.com.au, Domain), and internal master CRMs. 

Provision, test, and deploy complex server networks, cloud systems (Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory / Entra ID), and endpoint systems using modern Mobile Device Management (MDM) software. 

Formulate comprehensive testing strategies to validate network throughput, failover systems, and server redundancy, ensuring the agency maintains its strict zero-downtime metric during business hours. 

Provide expert troubleshooting and fault-finding services to isolate, diagnose, and resolve intricate network bugs, hardware failures, system anomalies, or cross-platform software conflicts. 

Troubleshoot complex issues across hardware, networks, software, database applications, servers, and workstations, coordinating with internal teams and vendors, and maintaining high service standards. 

Actively contribute to ZED Real Estate’s Information Security Management System (ISMS) by supporting the implementation and upkeep of its policies, procedures and controls, ensuring the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information in alignment with ISO/IEC?27001. 

Design and execute network security baselines, including Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), Zero-Trust conditional access rules, Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and advanced endpoint detection systems. 

Architect and manage Identity and Access Management (IAM) lifecycle workflows to enforce continuous security baselines across automated user onboarding and offboarding frameworks.

Strong analytical skills and sound administration skills
